articles.title: GMR Airports Is Approaching a Powerful Reversal Zone
articles.description: GMR Airports is once again trading near one of its most important long-term support zones. If we look at the weekly chart, the stock has been moving inside a broad rising channel for almost three years. Every time price approached the lower trendline, buyers stepped in and a strong recovery followed. On the other hand, the upper trendline has repeatedly acted as resistance. Now price has corrected from the 115–117 zone and returned towards the 90–92 support area where the rising trendline and 100 EMA are coming together. This confluence makes the current zone extremely interesting. The weekly RSI is also approaching the lower range near 38, suggesting momentum has weakened significantly during this correction. But the bigger structure is still intact as long as buyers continue defending this trendline. What makes this setup interesting is that the stock is approaching a zone where previous corrections turned into strong rallies. Weak hands may be exiting after the recent fall while long-term buyers could start accumulating near support. If price manages to hold above 90–92 and shows a strong weekly reversal, the first recovery could take it towards 105–110 followed by another attempt at the upper channel resistance near 118–120. A successful breakout above that resistance could open the door towards 130–135 and potentially start a much stronger expansion phase. The recent quarterly sales growth shown on the chart also adds a positive fundamental element, although price confirmation is still important. For now, the most important thing is whether buyers defend this support. If this three-year rising structure continues to hold, the current correction could become the foundation for the next major bullish leg.

articles.title: World Bank in Talks with Dozens of Countries about Crisis Aid, Banga Says
articles.description: The World Bank is in discussions with 30 to 40 countries about potential crisis aid to help them manage energy shocks and price increases triggered by the war in the Middle East, its president, Ajay Banga, told Reuters in an interview. Banga said the global economy had proven fairly resilient, in part due to big AI investments and adjustments in supply and demand for oil, which meant that few countries had sought the initial $25 billion in crisis funds that the World Bank had made available when the war began in late February.
